title: New HVAC training center opens as El Niño raises the stakes for cooling efficiency

blocks.text: The Philippines’ growing need for reliable cooling extends beyond homes and offices. As the country braces for a strong to very strong El Niño expected to persist into the first half of 2027, according to PAGASA, efficient air conditioning is also an important consideration for businesses and industries that depend on controlled temperatures and uninterrupted operations.

LG Electronics Philippines is expanding its focus on this market with the opening of its HVAC Academy and Business Innovation Center in Silver City, Pasig, on October 9. The facility combines technical training for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) professionals with demonstrations of LG’s commercial technologies, including systems designed for larger buildings and industrial applications.

The opening comes as LG looks to expand its commercial cooling business in the Philippines, where demand for data centers and other digital infrastructure is creating opportunities for more specialized HVAC systems.
Cooling becomes an industrial requirement

The importance of cooling is particularly evident in data centers, where temperature control is necessary to keep servers and other computing equipment operating reliably. As businesses expand their use of cloud services and artificial intelligence, facilities must manage the heat generated by increasingly demanding computing workloads.

LG Electronics Philippines sales manager Vanlee Budod told the media present that data centers have become a priority for the company’s global business. “Our main target, actually, LG Global’s main target right now are data centers,” Budod said.

The company expects demand for commercial and industrial cooling solutions to increase over the next one to two years as the Philippines develops its digital infrastructure. Beyond data centers, LG identifies semiconductor facilities, healthcare environments, commercial real estate, hospitality, and smart buildings as markets that require reliable and efficient HVAC systems.

El Niño adds another consideration for Philippine businesses. PAGASA’s October 7 advisory warned that the ongoing phenomenon could intensify into a very strong event and continue through the first half of 2027, increasing the likelihood of below-normal rainfall and dry spells or drought in some areas. While the effects will vary by location, businesses must contend with the operational demands of cooling in a country already exposed to high temperatures.

Energy efficiency is therefore relevant alongside cooling capacity. HVAC systems can account for a substantial share of a building’s energy use, depending on its design and operations. Equipment selection, proper installation, maintenance, and controls all affect how efficiently a system performs.
Training engineers for more complex systems

LG’s new HVAC Academy is designed to develop the technical skills needed to specify, install, commission, troubleshoot, and maintain these systems. Its training covers engineering design and simulation, advanced HVAC equipment, smart building controls, and cloud-based management.

The facility includes learning opportunities involving variable refrigerant flow (VRF) systems, heat pumps, chillers, and centralized controls. These technologies serve different applications, from individual commercial buildings to larger facilities with more demanding cooling requirements.

The emphasis on technical training reflects the work involved in keeping HVAC systems operating as intended. Selecting suitable equipment is only one part of the process. Poor installation, incorrect commissioning, or inadequate maintenance can undermine system performance, including its energy efficiency and reliability.

The academy is intended for mechanical contractors, consulting and specifying engineers, commissioning technicians, facilities managers, maintenance engineers, and LG’s own technical and business teams. The company also plans to use the facility to help customers understand how its equipment can be applied to their projects.

According to LG, the Pasig academy follows the opening of a similar facility in Cebu in 2025. Budod said that the company aims to hold at least four training sessions a week, accommodating around 10 to 20 participants per session. Training is offered free of charge, with some participants eligible for internal LG certification after completing the required assessment.
LG is also considering a partnership with the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority, although no formal agreement or timetable has been announced.
Beyond air conditioning

The Business Innovation Center, which shares the Pasig facility with the academy, showcases other parts of LG’s business-to-business portfolio. These include information displays for commercial, educational, and hospitality settings, IT solutions, and commercial laundry equipment.

The broader facility gives customers and industry professionals a place to examine LG technologies and discuss potential applications with the company’s teams. For its HVAC business, the academy also provides a venue for developing the technical knowledge required as cooling systems become more specialized.

LG is preparing for possible growth in the Philippine data center market as demand for AI and cloud services expands. Budod said the company was monitoring developments in the country’s participation in the US-led Pax Silica initiative, while emphasizing that LG was preparing for potential business opportunities rather than announcing a confirmed project.
“That’s their comment, but for us, we’re just preparing,” Budod affirmed

The company’s investment in training comes as cooling requirements extend across more sectors of the economy. For data centers, cooling supports the operation of computing infrastructure. For commercial buildings and industrial facilities, it affects equipment reliability, working conditions, and energy consumption. Developing the workforce capable of designing and maintaining these systems will be part of meeting that demand.
